newsitem.title: USA: Phillips' net up 38 percent on higher oil prices.
newsitem.headline: Phillips' net up 38 percent on higher oil prices.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co. said Wednesday that third-quarter earnings rose 38 percent, as surging prices for crude oil and natural gas more than offset rising refining costs and weak chemical results.

Phillips is the latest major oil company to report higher earnings fuelled by rising oil prices. On Monday, Texaco Inc. said earnings jumped 50 percent in the quarter, Chevron Corp. posted a 29 percent gain excluding special items and Exxon Corp., the nation's largest oil company, said profits rose 4 percent.

Bartlesville, Okla.-based Phillips said net income rose to $187 million, or 71 cents a share, in the quarter, from $136 million, or 52 cents a share, for the same period last year. Sales rose 14 percent to $3.85 billion from $3.37 billion.
"These results continue a trend of strong quarterly earnings in 1996, setting the stage for an outstanding year," Chairman Wayne Allen said in a statement.
Operating earnings in exploration and production nearly doubled as Phillips' average oil price rose $4.90 to $20.54 a barrel and natural gas prices jumped 49 percent.
Natural gas production rose 4 percent while crude oil production was flat worldwide, Phillips said.
Refining and marketing earnings fell slightly, as the costs of crude oil feedstock were higher.
Chemical profits fell significantly from last year's strong results, primarily due to lower margins for ethylene, a gas derived from natural gas, and other products.
Phillips stock fell 25 cents to $42.125 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
